claims.statement: `app/(dashboard)/tenant-scope.ts` lives in `app/` only because it joins `modules/auth`'s and `modules/tenancy`'s private `data/` layers, which no module may cross (rule 8); the rule it applies lives in `modules/tenancy/domain/scope.ts`.

`getSignedInProfile` and `resolveRouteScope` are `cache()`-wrapped so the `/t/[tenantCode]` layout and its page share one `getProfileSnapshot` read per request; the underlying profile query is itself `cache()`d by `clerkUserId`, and `cache()` is per-request, so the wrapper dedupes rather than caches stale data.

`getSignedInProfile` collapses a failed identity read or any non-`ok` snapshot other than `not-found` to `'unknown'`, and `not-found` to `'none'`; `resolveRouteScope` checks `'unknown'` before `'none'` so 'we could not check' never renders as 'never assigned a school'.

`resolveRouteScope` has four arms — `ok`, `not-a-member`, `no-tenant-access`, `unknown` — and only `ok` yields a `TenantScope`; the segment layout renders the other three, and a foreign code never falls back to 'all schools'.

`scopeForCode` lowercases both sides and returns `null` unless the code matches a membership; a `TenantScope` is only built from `profile.tenants`, which is RLS-scoped, so the downstream `tenant_id = scope.tenantId` filter selects among schools RLS already allows rather than granting.

`requireScope` returns `null` instead of calling `notFound()` because layouts and pages render in parallel and a thrown 404 could race the layout's more specific state; every page under the segment starts with the `if (!resolved) return null` guard.

`resolveTrustedRole` reads `profiles.role` only — the column RLS reads — and is the function redirects and authorization decisions must call; it is async for signature stability while its body is the synchronous `asResolvedRole`.

`resolveRouteRole` prefers the unauthenticated `?role=` override ahead of the trusted role, so it is a presentation signal: any caller can set it and a real trainer adding `?role=admin` would skip an office-only redirect.

`toOfficeRole` narrows every non-office role — an unparsed string, `null`, `trainer` — to read-only `viewer`, and `tests/unit/display-role.test.ts` pins that as a least-privilege rule rather than a cosmetic default.

Billing and report redirect trainers on `resolveTrustedRole` before the batch fetch so no billing figure is serialized into a trainer's payload (rule 5), and `users/new` prefers it over any override because its Clerk-invitation branch has no RLS behind it.

`withTenantAccess` rewrites only an `ok` snapshot to `no-tenant-access`, leaving `sync-failed` and `unconfigured` untouched so a tidier membership explanation never masks a real fetch failure; `unknown` changes nothing.
The shell layout uses `resolveTrustedRole` for the admin-only 'Add user' nav row — hiding only, with the route and Server Action re-checking the same role.

Rule 2 permits a `tenant_id = scope.tenantId` filter taken from a validated `TenantScope` and bans a JS tenant check used as access control; the workflow's mistakes therefore mislead rather than leak, because RLS (rule 1) remains the boundary under every step.

`requireScope` performs the trainer redirect itself — after narrowing to the `ok` arm and `return`ing `null` on every other arm — by comparing `resolved.profile.role === 'trainer'` and calling `redirect('/trainer')`, so no office page starts its fetch for a trainer and rule 5's server-side omission holds structurally rather than per route.

The trainer gate is in the page path rather than the segment layout because a layout does not re-run on every client-side navigation, and it fires only after the `ok` narrowing so a trainer on a foreign school code gets the layout's 'School not available' state instead of a bounce to `/trainer`.

Because `requireScope` already redirects trainers, the surviving `if (trustedRole === 'trainer') redirect('/trainer')` blocks in `billing/page.tsx`, `report/page.tsx` and the school dashboard are redundant second guards rather than the load-bearing gate.

The trainer gate survives a `?role=` override: a real trainer requesting `/t/<school>/billing?role=admin` is still redirected, because the redirect reads the database role while `?role=` only reaches `resolveRouteRole` → `toOfficeRole`/`resolveDisplayRole` on a page already rendering; gating the redirect on `resolveRouteRole` is what would break it.

`resolveDisplayRole` picks a presentation variant, preferring a recognised `?role=` office role and otherwise narrowing the trusted role, so `?role=trainer` cannot select a trainer variant; `tests/unit/display-role.test.ts` pins that alongside the least-privilege `viewer` fallback.

Screens holding a profile from `requireScope` fold `tenantAccessOf(profile)` into `withTenantAccess`, start with the `if (!resolved) return null` guard, and derive their render role from the trusted role (`toOfficeRole(await resolveTrustedRole(profile.role))`) with no second profile read — all eight pages under `/t/[tenantCode]` call `requireScope`.

`app_private.current_role()` — the function every role-checking policy calls — selects `profiles.role` from the row that `app_private.current_profile_id()` resolves from the JWT `sub`, so a role decision made on any other column can disagree with the database that enforces it; Clerk is identity only.

The single `batches` UPDATE policy is `can_manage_tenant` on both `using` and `with check`, i.e. admin/coordinator of the tenant only, so a viewer write matches zero rows — visible in the UI as `conflict-or-denied` rather than as a silent success.

The tenant Server Action re-resolves the school from the `tenantCode` form field against the caller's own memberships (never taking a tenant id from the form), requires a trusted `admin`/`coordinator` via `resolveTrustedRole`, and returns a save failure for `unknown` while returning `denied` for any other non-`ok` scope outcome.

`batch-cards/page.tsx` renders the RQM editor only for a trusted `admin`/`coordinator` and passes it into the client view, so `viewer` and any unresolved role get a read-only card — usability only, since the action re-checks and the `batches` UPDATE policy refuses the write.

`deriveTrainerMetrics` strips `nextBilling`, `openBillingObligations`, `billingDeadlinesMissing` and `overdueBilling` out of the shared summary by destructuring, so billing keys are absent from the object a trainer's page serializes, not merely unrendered.

`trainer/page.tsx` calls the unscoped `getBatchesSnapshot()` and lets RLS's `can_read_batch` limit it to batches assigned to the caller — no tenant scope, no billing fields, and no role check of its own.

`resolveDisplayRole` has no live caller in `app/`: the only page resolving a preview role is billing, which calls `resolveRouteRole` then `toOfficeRole`, so `resolveDisplayRole` survives as the tested composition of those two halves rather than part of the request path.

`Profile.role` is typed as the shared `UserRole` that `modules/auth/data/role.ts` resolves against, so a second role vocabulary cannot appear without a type error; the profile module also carries `hasTenantMembership` for membership-by-id questions.

`/dashboard` dispatches on `profile.role` alone before falling through to the scoped legacy redirect — trainers to `/trainer`, admins to `/overview` — so the trusted column, not a resolver, decides each role's landing route.

`/overview` gates on `(await resolveTrustedRole(profile.role)) !== 'admin'` and redirects anyone else to `/dashboard`, treating `unknown` as a rendered retry state instead — an `unknown` profile never falls through to `none`'s redirect.
